name: Headache
summary: Many headaches improve with time, fluids, rest and avoiding common triggers.
self_care: Drink water regularly.
Rest if you are unwell and try to reduce stress.
Avoid skipping meals and avoid alcohol while the headache is active.
A pharmacist can advise whether an over-the-counter pain reliever is suitable for you.
urgent: Headache with vomiting, vision problems, or symptoms that are worsening or repeatedly returning should be assessed urgently.
emergency: A sudden extremely painful headache, seizure, new weakness/numbness, difficulty speaking/walking, confusion, loss of vision, or a stiff neck with a very high temperature needs emergency assessment.

name: Cough
summary: A new cough often improves on its own, but breathing difficulty, chest pain or coughing blood need medical assessment.
self_care: Rest and drink plenty of fluids.
Warm lemon and honey may soothe a cough for people over 1 year old.
A pharmacist can advise on symptom-relief products and whether they are suitable for you.
urgent: Seek urgent advice if the cough becomes very bad, you feel very unwell, have chest pain, have difficulty breathing, or cough up blood.
emergency: Severe breathing difficulty or other life-threatening symptoms require emergency help.

name: Sore throat
summary: Sore throats are common and often improve within about a week.
self_care: Drink water and choose cool or soft foods if they are easier to swallow.
Adults and older children can consider warm salt-water gargles if safe for them.
Rest and avoid smoking or smoky places.
A pharmacist can advise on pain relief or medicated lozenges.
urgent: Very high temperature, dehydration, weakened immunity, or symptoms that do not improve should be assessed.
emergency: Difficulty breathing, inability to swallow, drooling, stridor, or rapidly worsening severe symptoms need emergency help.

name: Diarrhoea or vomiting
summary: The main priority is preventing dehydration and watching for signs that need urgent review.
self_care: Take frequent small sips of fluid if you feel sick.
Rest and eat when you feel able.
A pharmacist can advise about oral rehydration products and whether other medicines are appropriate.
urgent: Seek urgent advice if you cannot keep fluids down, have signs of dehydration, bloody diarrhoea, or symptoms lasting longer than expected.
emergency: Vomiting blood, severe sudden abdominal pain, severe breathing difficulty, confusion, or being unresponsive needs emergency help.

name: High temperature / fever
summary: A high temperature in adults is commonly defined as 38°C or above, although how you feel also matters.
self_care: Rest and drink enough fluid to avoid dehydration.
Monitor how you feel and seek advice if symptoms worsen or you are concerned.
A pharmacist can advise on suitable over-the-counter symptom relief.
urgent: Persistent or worsening fever, severe dehydration, significant vulnerability, or concerning associated symptoms should be reviewed.
emergency: Fever with severe breathing difficulty, confusion, a seizure, a non-fading rash, or a stiff neck with severe headache needs emergency assessment.

name: Chest pain
summary: Chest pain has many causes and should not be self-diagnosed.
self_care: Do not rely on home treatment to rule out a serious cause of new chest pain.
urgent: Chest pain that comes and goes, or pain that has settled but still worries you, should be medically assessed.
emergency: Sudden chest pain or pressure that does not go away, pain spreading to an arm/neck/jaw/back, or chest pain with sweating, sickness, light-headedness or shortness of breath needs emergency help.

name: Shortness of breath
summary: Breathlessness can be serious and should not be self-diagnosed.
self_care: If breathlessness is new, worsening or unexplained, seek medical advice rather than relying on home treatment.
urgent: Contact urgent medical services if breathing is more difficult than usual, or if breathlessness is associated with coughing blood, leg swelling or palpitations.
emergency: Severe breathing difficulty, gasping/choking, inability to speak full sentences, chest tightness/heaviness, pale/blue/grey lips or skin, or sudden confusion needs emergency help.

name: Allergic reaction
summary: Allergic reactions can range from mild symptoms to anaphylaxis.
self_care: Avoid a suspected trigger if you can do so safely.
For mild allergy symptoms, a pharmacist can advise whether an antihistamine or other treatment is suitable.
urgent: If you are unsure whether symptoms are becoming more serious, seek urgent medical advice.
emergency: Sudden swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue; severe breathing difficulty; throat tightness; fainting; or marked confusion can be signs of anaphylaxis and need emergency help.
